renders._yaml:
- component: card
  title: Share of counts removed as ambient
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median fraction of all counts that CellBender called ambient RNA and removed, over the samples in view. It answers how much of the signal was background.
    How to read: a small fraction means a clean sample and little change to the matrix. A large one means heavy ambient contamination, so compare samples and look at the CellBender report of the outlier before using its matrix.
    Note: CellBender documents no cut-off for this fraction, so no pass mark is drawn. It depends on the target false-positive rate the run used.
    Source: https://cellbender.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage/index.html
  column: fraction_counts_removed
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with the lowest and highest sample

- component: card
  title: Cells found per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of barcodes CellBender kept as cells, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how many cells each sample yielded after background removal.
    How to read: samples of the same design should give similar counts. A sample far below or above its peers was either filtered hard or called many empty droplets, so check it against its UMI curve.
    Source: https://cellbender.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage/index.html
  column: found_cells
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Found against expected cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ratio of cells CellBender found to cells it expected, over the samples in view. It answers whether the called cell count matches the prior the run started from.
    How to read: a ratio near 1 means the call agrees with the expectation, and CellBender asks only for an expected-cells value within a factor of 2. A ratio far outside that means the setting did not match the data or the cell call went wrong, so compare it with the UMI curve as the CellBender troubleshooting guide advises.
    Note: CellBender defines no acceptable range for this ratio, so no pass mark is drawn.
    Sources: https://cellbender.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/index.html and https://cellbender.readthedocs.io/en/latest/troubleshooting/index.html
  column: ratio_of_found_cells_to_expected_cells
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with the lowest and highest sample

- component: table
  title: Ambient-RNA removal per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, with the counts before and after removal, the fraction removed, the expected and found cell counts and the target false-positive rate. It answers the exact numbers behind the cards.
    How to read: sort by the fraction removed to find the most contaminated samples, then check the found-to-expected ratio of the same row.
